Title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
authors: Shunyu Yao and Jeffrey Zhao and Dian Yu and others
Abstract: We explore the use of large language models to generate both reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner thereby allowing greater synergy between the two. This approach called ReAct is a simple yet effective method that outperforms prior state-of-the-art results across diverse benchmarks.

Title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
authors: Noah Shinn and Federico Cassano and Ashwin Gopinath and others
Abstract: Reflexion is an approach to reinforce language agents by having them evaluate task success and use the resulting self-reflection to improve their future attempts.

Title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
authors: Shunyu Yao and Dian Yu and Jeffrey Zhao and others
Abstract: We introduce Tree of Thoughts ToT a framework that generalizes over Chain-of-Thought prompting and enables exploration over coherent units of text that serve as intermediate steps toward problem solving.

Title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Overcoming Step-by-Step Large Language Model Prompting Failures
authors: Lei Wang and Wanyu Xu and Yihuai Lan and others
Abstract: Plan-and-Solve prompt is a method to improve the planning ability of large language models for complex reasoning tasks. It decomposes a task into a plan and then executes the plan step by step.

Title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning Acting and Planning in Language Models
authors: Andy Zhou and Kai Yan and Michal Shlapentokh-Rothman and others
Abstract: Language Agent Tree Search LATS combines language models with Monte Carlo tree search and self-reflective feedback to enable deliberate structured reasoning and acting.

Title: An Emacs Blog Post on Prompt Engineering for LLMs
Abstract: A personal blog post discussing practical tips for prompting large language models and building agentic workflows.
